questions.prompt: How many protons are in ^56Fe^3+? Enter the number only.
hints: The proton count is what makes it iron.
questions.explanation: The element is iron, so Z = 26. Every iron atom and ion has 26 protons.

questions.prompt: How many neutrons are in ^56Fe^3+? Enter the number only.
hints: Neutrons = mass number - atomic number.
questions.explanation: Neutrons = A - Z = 56 - 26 = 30.

commonErrors.message: That is the proton count. Subtract it from the mass number 56 to get neutrons.
commonErrors.label: used-atomic-number

commonErrors.message: That is the mass number, which counts protons AND neutrons together.
commonErrors.label: used-mass-number

questions.prompt: How many electrons are in ^56Fe^3+? Enter the number only.
hints: A positive charge means electrons were lost, not gained.
questions.explanation: A neutral Fe atom has 26 electrons. The 3+ charge means three were removed: 26 - 3 = 23.

commonErrors.message: A 3+ charge means the ion LOST three electrons, so subtract rather than add.
commonErrors.label: charge-sign-flipped

commonErrors.message: That is the neutral atom. This species carries a 3+ charge.
commonErrors.label: ignored-charge

questions.prompt: A species has 34 protons, 45 neutrons and 36 electrons. Which element is it? Give the name or the symbol.
hints: Only one of the three counts identifies the element.
questions.explanation: The proton count alone fixes the identity: Z = 34 is selenium.

questions.prompt: A species has 34 protons, 45 neutrons and 36 electrons. What is its mass number? Enter the number only.
hints: Mass number counts the particles in the nucleus.
questions.explanation: A = protons + neutrons = 34 + 45 = 79. Electrons contribute no measurable mass.

commonErrors.message: Electrons are not counted in the mass number. Add protons and neutrons only.
commonErrors.label: counted-electrons

questions.prompt: A species has 34 protons, 45 neutrons and 36 electrons. What is its charge? Enter a signed number, such as -2 or 3.
hints: Compare the number of protons with the number of electrons.
questions.explanation: Charge = protons - electrons = 34 - 36 = -2.

commonErrors.message: Check the sign. Extra electrons give a NEGATIVE charge.
commonErrors.label: charge-sign-flipped

questions.prompt: How many electrons are in ^31P^3-? Enter the number only.
hints: A negative charge means electrons were gained.
questions.explanation: Phosphorus has Z = 15. The 3- charge means three electrons were gained: 15 + 3 = 18.

commonErrors.message: A 3- charge means the ion GAINED three electrons, so add rather than subtract.
commonErrors.label: charge-sign-flipped

questions.prompt: How many neutrons are in a neutral atom of ^238U? Enter the number only.
hints: Look up the atomic number of uranium first.
questions.explanation: Uranium has Z = 92, so neutrons = 238 - 92 = 146.

questions.prompt: Copper has two isotopes: Cu-63 (62.9296 amu, 69.15%) and Cu-65 (64.9278 amu, 30.85%). What is the average atomic mass in amu? Enter the number only.
hints: Convert each percentage to a decimal fraction first.
Multiply each isotopic mass by its fraction, then add the two products.

commonErrors.message: You took a plain average. Each isotope must be weighted by its abundance.
commonErrors.label: unweighted-average

questions.prompt: Gallium averages 69.723 amu and has two isotopes, Ga-69 (68.926 amu) and Ga-71 (70.925 amu). What is the percent abundance of **Ga-69**?
hints: Call the Ga-69 fraction x. The Ga-71 fraction is then (1 - x).
Set up 68.926x + 70.925(1 - x) = 69.723 and solve for x.

commonErrors.message: That is the Ga-71 abundance. The question asks for Ga-69, the lighter isotope.
commonErrors.label: wrong-isotope-reported

commonErrors.message: The average sits closer to 69 than to 71, so the two isotopes cannot be equally abundant.
commonErrors.label: assumed-equal-abundance

questions.prompt: Element X has two isotopes: X-10 (10.013 amu, 19.9%) and X-11 (11.009 amu, 80.1%). What is its average atomic mass in amu? Enter the number only.
hints: The answer must fall between 10.013 and 11.009, and closer to the more abundant one.
questions.explanation: (10.013)(0.199) = 1.99 and (11.009)(0.801) = 8.82. Adding gives 10.81 amu, which identifies boron.

questions.prompt: Silver has two isotopes: Ag-107 (106.905 amu, 51.84%) and Ag-109 (108.905 amu, 48.16%). What is the average atomic mass in amu? Enter the number only.
hints: Multiply each mass by its fraction, then add the products.
questions.explanation: (106.905)(0.5184) = 55.42 and (108.905)(0.4816) = 52.45. Adding gives 107.87 amu, exactly the periodic table value.

questions.prompt: Chlorine averages 35.453 amu with isotopes Cl-35 (34.969 amu) and Cl-37 (36.966 amu). What is the percent abundance of **Cl-35**?
hints: Set up the weighted average with x as the Cl-35 fraction.
The average lies much nearer 35 than 37, so expect x well above 0.5.

commonErrors.message: That is the Cl-37 abundance. Since 35.453 sits close to 35, the lighter isotope must be the abundant one.
commonErrors.label: wrong-isotope-reported

questions.prompt: Lithium has two isotopes: Li-6 (6.015 amu, 7.59%) and Li-7 (7.016 amu, 92.41%). What is the average atomic mass in amu? Enter the number only.
hints: Li-7 dominates, so the answer should land very close to 7.016.

questions.prompt: Rubidium has two isotopes: Rb-85 (84.912 amu, 72.17%) and Rb-87 (86.909 amu, 27.83%). What is the average atomic mass in amu? Enter the number only.
hints: Weight each isotopic mass by its own abundance before adding.

questions.prompt: What is the molar mass of Ca(NO_3)_2?
hints: The subscript 2 outside the parentheses multiplies everything inside.
questions.explanation: 40.08 + 2(14.01) + 6(16.00) = 40.08 + 28.02 + 96.00 = 164.10 g/mol. The 2 outside the parentheses multiplies the nitrogen AND the three oxygens, giving 6 oxygens rather than 3.

commonErrors.message: You distributed the 2 to nitrogen but not to oxygen. There are 6 oxygen atoms, not 3.
commonErrors.label: subscript-not-distributed

commonErrors.message: The 2 outside the parentheses was ignored entirely. Each formula unit holds 2 nitrate ions.
commonErrors.label: subscript-ignored

questions.prompt: What is the molar mass of (NH_4)_3PO_4?
hints: The subscript 3 multiplies the whole ammonium ion: 3 N and 12 H.

commonErrors.message: The 3 outside the parentheses was ignored. There are 3 ammonium ions per formula unit.
commonErrors.label: subscript-ignored

questions.prompt: What is the molar mass of Al_2(SO_4)_3?
hints: Three sulfate ions contribute 3 S and 12 O.
questions.explanation: 2(26.98) + 3(32.06) + 12(16.00) = 53.96 + 96.18 + 192.00 = 342.14 g/mol. Three sulfate ions carry 12 oxygen atoms between them.

commonErrors.message: The 3 must reach the oxygens too. Three sulfates carry 12 oxygen atoms, not 4.
commonErrors.label: subscript-not-distributed

questions.prompt: What is the molar mass of Mg_3(PO_4)_2?
hints: Two phosphate ions carry 2 P and 8 O.

questions.prompt: What is the molar mass of C_9H_8O_4 (aspirin)?
hints: Nothing tricky here, just careful addition.
questions.explanation: 9(12.01) + 8(1.008) + 4(16.00) = 108.09 + 8.064 + 64.00 = 180.15 g/mol. No parentheses and no hydrate here; the only real risk is dropping a digit.

questions.prompt: What is the molar mass of Fe_2(SO_4)_3?
hints: Same shape as aluminium sulfate: 3 S and 12 O.
questions.explanation: 2(55.85) + 3(32.06) + 12(16.00) = 111.70 + 96.18 + 192.00 = 399.88 g/mol. Same shape as aluminium sulfate: three sulfates give 12 oxygens.

commonErrors.message: Distribute the 3 across the entire sulfate ion, giving 12 oxygens.
commonErrors.label: subscript-not-distributed

questions.prompt: What is the molar mass of (NH_4)_2Cr_2O_7?
hints: Two ammonium ions give 2 N and 8 H; the dichromate gives 2 Cr and 7 O.
questions.explanation: 2(14.01) + 8(1.008) + 2(52.00) + 7(16.00) = 28.02 + 8.064 + 104.00 + 112.00 = 252.08 g/mol. Two ammonium ions give 2 N and 8 H; the dichromate gives 2 Cr and 7 O.

questions.prompt: How many moles are in 45.0 g of NaCl?
hints: Molar mass goes in the denominator so that grams cancel.

commonErrors.message: You multiplied by the molar mass instead of dividing. Check that grams cancel in your setup.
commonErrors.label: inverted-conversion-factor

questions.prompt: What is the mass of 2.50 mol of C_6H_12O_6?
hints: Moles times molar mass gives grams.
Three significant figures on 450 is ambiguous. Write 4.50 x 10^2 instead.
questions.explanation: 2.50 mol x 180.16 g/mol = 450. g, best written 4.50 x 10^2 g so the three significant figures are unambiguous.

questions.prompt: How many moles are in 12.0 g of He?
hints: Helium is monatomic, so its molar mass is just the atomic mass.
questions.explanation: 12.0 g / 4.003 g/mol = 3.00 mol. Report all three digits.

questions.prompt: What is the mass of 0.0350 mol of Al_2(SO_4)_3?
hints: Leading zeros never count. How many significant figures does 0.0350 have?
Round the raw product 11.975 to three significant figures.
questions.explanation: 0.0350 mol x 342.14 g/mol = 11.975 g. The leading zeros are not significant, so 0.0350 carries three significant figures and the answer rounds to 12.0 g.

questions.prompt: How many moles are in 500.0 g of CaCO_3?
hints: A trailing zero after a decimal point IS significant.
500.0 carries four significant figures, so your answer should too.
questions.explanation: 500.0 / 100.09 = 4.9955 mol. The trailing decimal zero makes 500.0 a four significant figure value, so report 4.996 mol.

questions.prompt: What is the mass of 0.250 mol of Ca(NO_3)_2?
hints: Work out the molar mass first, remembering the 6 oxygens.

questions.prompt: How many moles are in 88.0 g of CO_2?
hints: The molar mass of CO_2 is close to 44, so expect roughly 2 mol.

questions.prompt: What is the mass of 1.75 mol of NH_3?
How many molecules are in 25.0 g of CO_2?
hints: Grams to moles first. Avogadro's number never touches grams directly.
n = 0.568 mol

commonErrors.message: You skipped the molar mass step. Convert grams to moles before using Avogadro's number.
commonErrors.label: skipped-molar-mass

questions.prompt: What is the mass of 3.50 x 10^22 atoms of Fe?
hints: Divide by Avogadro's number to reach moles, then multiply by molar mass.

questions.prompt: How many molecules are in 1.00 g of H_2O?
hints: One gram is well under a mole, so expect an exponent below 23.

questions.prompt: What is the mass of 5.00 x 10^20 molecules of NaCl?
hints: Ionic compounds are counted in molecules, but the arithmetic is identical.

questions.prompt: How many atoms are in 100.0 g of Ar?
hints: Argon is monatomic, so atoms and particles are the same thing here.

questions.prompt: How many atoms are in 2.00 g of He?
hints: Two grams of helium is about half a mole.

questions.prompt: What is the mass of 1.20 x 10^24 molecules of H_2O?
hints: That count is just under two moles.

questions.prompt: How many oxygen atoms are in 50.0 g of Ca(NO_3)_2?
hints: How many oxygen atoms are in ONE formula unit?
Multiply the moles of compound by 6 before reaching for Avogadro's number.
questions.explanation: 50.0 / 164.10 = 0.3047 mol. Each formula unit holds 6 oxygens, so x 6 = 1.828 mol O, then x 6.022 x 10^23 = 1.10 x 10^24 atoms.

commonErrors.message: That is the number of formula units. Each one contains 6 oxygen atoms, so multiply by 6.
commonErrors.label: subscript-step-skipped

commonErrors.message: You used 3 oxygens. The subscript 2 outside the parentheses doubles the nitrate, giving 6.
commonErrors.label: subscript-not-distributed

questions.prompt: How many hydrogen atoms are in 10.0 g of C_6H_12O_6?
hints: Glucose carries 12 hydrogens per molecule.
questions.explanation: 10.0 / 180.16 = 0.05551 mol. Each molecule holds 12 H, so x 12 = 0.6661 mol H, then x 6.022 x 10^23 = 4.01 x 10^23 atoms.

commonErrors.message: That is the number of glucose molecules. Multiply by 12 to count hydrogen atoms.
commonErrors.label: subscript-step-skipped

questions.prompt: How many TOTAL atoms are in 5.00 g of NH_3?
hints: Count every atom in one NH_3 molecule, nitrogen included.
questions.explanation: 5.00 / 17.03 = 0.2936 mol. Each molecule holds 4 atoms (1 N + 3 H), so x 4 = 1.174 mol atoms, then x 6.022 x 10^23 = 7.07 x 10^23 atoms.

commonErrors.message: That counts molecules, not atoms. Each molecule contains 4 atoms.
commonErrors.label: molecules-reported-as-atoms

commonErrors.message: You counted only the hydrogens. 'Total atoms' includes the nitrogen.
commonErrors.label: nitrogen-omitted

questions.prompt: What mass of Al_2(SO_4)_3 contains 1.50 x 10^23 sulfur atoms?
hints: Running the chain backwards means the subscript step DIVIDES instead of multiplying.
0.249 mol S corresponds to 0.0830 mol of compound.
questions.explanation: 1.50 x 10^23 / 6.022 x 10^23 = 0.2491 mol S. There are 3 S per formula unit, so divide: 0.08303 mol compound, then x 342.14 g/mol = 28.4 g.

commonErrors.message: You skipped the 3 S per formula unit. Divide the moles of sulfur by 3 before converting to mass.
commonErrors.label: subscript-step-skipped

commonErrors.message: You multiplied by 3 where you needed to divide. Three sulfur atoms come from ONE formula unit.
commonErrors.label: subscript-step-inverted

questions.prompt: How many oxygen atoms are in 25.00 g of CuSO_4*5H_2O?
hints: The waters contain oxygen too.
There are 9 oxygen atoms per formula unit, not 4.
questions.explanation: 25.00 / 249.69 = 0.1001 mol. Oxygen appears in the sulfate AND the five waters: 4 + 5 = 9 per formula unit. So x 9 = 0.9011 mol O, then x 6.022 x 10^23 = 5.427 x 10^23 atoms.

commonErrors.message: You counted only the sulfate oxygens. The five waters carry 5 more, giving 9 in total.
commonErrors.label: hydrate-oxygen-missed

questions.prompt: How many nitrogen atoms are in 20.0 g of (NH_4)_3PO_4?
hints: The subscript 3 outside the parentheses sets the nitrogen count.
questions.explanation: 20.0 / 149.10 = 0.1341 mol. Three ammonium ions give 3 N per formula unit, so x 3 = 0.4024 mol N, then x 6.022 x 10^23 = 2.42 x 10^23 atoms.

commonErrors.message: That is the number of formula units. Each holds 3 nitrogen atoms.
commonErrors.label: subscript-step-skipped

questions.prompt: How many oxygen atoms are in 0.500 mol of Mg_3(PO_4)_2?
hints: You are already in moles, so no molar mass is needed. Just the subscript step and Avogadro.
questions.explanation: Two phosphate ions carry 8 oxygens, so 0.500 x 8 = 4.00 mol O, then x 6.022 x 10^23 = 2.41 x 10^24 atoms.

commonErrors.message: Distribute the 2 outside the parentheses: two phosphates carry 8 oxygens, not 4.
commonErrors.label: subscript-not-distributed

questions.prompt: How many TOTAL atoms are in 15.0 g of Ca(NO_3)_2?
hints: Add up every atom in one formula unit before converting.
questions.explanation: 15.0 / 164.10 = 0.09141 mol. Each formula unit holds 1 Ca + 2 N + 6 O = 9 atoms, so x 9 = 0.8227 mol atoms, then x 6.022 x 10^23 = 4.95 x 10^23 atoms.

commonErrors.message: That counts formula units. Each contains 9 atoms in total.
commonErrors.label: subscript-step-skipped

questions.prompt: What is the mass percent of nitrogen in NH_4NO_3?
hints: There are two nitrogen atoms in ammonium nitrate, one in each ion.

commonErrors.message: You counted one nitrogen. Ammonium nitrate has one in NH_4^+ and one in NO_3^-.
commonErrors.label: counted-one-nitrogen

questions.prompt: What is the mass percent of calcium in CaCO_3?
hints: Mass of the part over mass of the whole.

questions.prompt: Calcium citrate is Ca_3(C_6H_5O_7)_2. What is its mass percent of calcium?
hints: Build the molar mass carefully: the 2 outside the parentheses doubles the entire citrate ion.
questions.explanation: Three calciums give 120.24 g out of 498.44 g/mol, so (120.24 / 498.44) x 100 = 24.12%. This is why a citrate tablet is physically larger than a carbonate one for the same labelled dose.

questions.prompt: What is the mass percent of carbon in aspirin, C_9H_8O_4?
hints: M(aspirin) = 180.15 g/mol.

questions.prompt: What is the mass percent of hydrogen in aspirin, C_9H_8O_4?
hints: Hydrogen is light, so expect a small percentage even though there are 8 of them.

questions.prompt: What is the mass percent of iron in Fe_2O_3?
hints: Both iron atoms count toward the numerator.

questions.prompt: You calculate the percent composition of a compound and your three percentages sum to 100.01%. What does that mean?

options: You made an arithmetic error and must redo it
Nothing is wrong; each percentage was rounded independently
The formula you were given must be incorrect
You should scale all three values down so they sum to exactly 100

hints: Think about what happens when you round three numbers separately and then add them.
questions.explanation: Rounding each percentage separately lets the total drift a hundredth either way. A sum of 100.01% or 99.99% is expected. A sum of 96% or 104% signals a real error, such as a dropped or double-counted element.

questions.prompt: A red laser emits light with a wavelength of 650. nm. What is its frequency in Hz? Enter the number only.
hints: Rearrange c = (wavelength)(frequency) to solve for frequency.
Nanometres must become metres before you divide: 1 nm = 10^-9 m.
questions.explanation: Convert to metres first: 650. nm = 6.50 x 10^-7 m. Then frequency = c / wavelength = 2.998 x 10^8 / 6.50 x 10^-7 = 4.61 x 10^14 Hz.

commonErrors.message: You divided by 650 without converting nanometres to metres. 650. nm = 6.50 x 10^-7 m.
commonErrors.label: no-unit-conversion

questions.prompt: A radio station broadcasts at 98.5 MHz. What is the wavelength of the signal in metres?
hints: Convert megahertz to hertz before dividing.
Radio waves are long, so expect an answer of a few metres.
questions.explanation: 1 MHz = 10^6 Hz, so 98.5 MHz = 9.85 x 10^7 Hz. Then wavelength = c / frequency = 2.998 x 10^8 / 9.85 x 10^7 = 3.04 m.

questions.prompt: What is the energy of a single photon of blue light with a wavelength of 450. nm, in joules?
hints: You can combine the two constants: hc = 1.986 x 10^-25 J m.
Remember to convert 450. nm into metres.
questions.explanation: Energy = hc / wavelength = (6.626 x 10^-34)(2.998 x 10^8) / 4.50 x 10^-7 = 1.986 x 10^-25 / 4.50 x 10^-7 = 4.41 x 10^-19 J. A single photon carries very little energy, so a negative exponent is the expected shape.

questions.prompt: A photon has a frequency of 6.50 x 10^14 Hz. What is its energy in joules?
hints: This one is a single multiplication: E = h times frequency.
questions.explanation: Energy = h x frequency = (6.626 x 10^-34)(6.50 x 10^14) = 4.31 x 10^-19 J. No wavelength conversion is needed here because the frequency was given directly.

questions.prompt: A photon carries 3.60 x 10^-19 J of energy. What is its wavelength in nanometres?
hints: Solve E = hc / wavelength for the wavelength.
Your answer in metres will be about 5.5 x 10^-7; convert that to nanometres.
questions.explanation: Rearranging E = hc / wavelength gives wavelength = hc / E = 1.986 x 10^-25 / 3.60 x 10^-19 = 5.518 x 10^-7 m. Multiplying by 10^9 converts that to 552 nm, which is green light.

questions.prompt: Write the full electron configuration of a neutral calcium atom (Z = 20).
hints: Follow the filling order and stop when the superscripts total 20.
After 3p^6 the next sublevel to fill is 4s, not 3d.
questions.explanation: Filling in order gives 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^2, and the superscripts add to 20. The condensed form [Ar] 4s^2 is also accepted.

questions.prompt: Write the noble-gas (condensed) electron configuration of a neutral bromine atom (Z = 35).
hints: Start from the noble gas that comes before bromine in the periodic table.
After 4s^2 the 3d sublevel fills before 4p.
questions.explanation: Argon accounts for the first 18 electrons, leaving 17 more: 4s^2 3d^10 4p^5. Writing 3d before 4s is also accepted, since textbooks differ on whether to list by filling order or by energy level.

questions.prompt: How many valence electrons does a neutral sulfur atom (Z = 16) have? Enter the number only.
hints: Write the configuration first, then count only the electrons in the highest n.
questions.explanation: Sulfur is [Ne] 3s^2 3p^4. The valence electrons are those in the outermost energy level, n = 3, giving 2 + 4 = 6. This also matches its group number.

commonErrors.message: That is the total electron count. Valence electrons are only those in the outermost energy level.
commonErrors.label: counted-all-electrons

commonErrors.message: You counted only the 3p electrons. The 3s pair is in the same energy level and counts too.
commonErrors.label: omitted-s-electrons

questions.prompt: Write the electron configuration of the Fe^2+ ion (iron is Z = 26).
hints: Write the neutral atom first, then remove two electrons.
For transition metals the outermost s electrons are the ones lost first.
questions.explanation: Neutral iron is [Ar] 4s^2 3d^6. When a transition metal is ionised the 4s electrons leave FIRST, even though 4s filled first, so removing two gives [Ar] 3d^6 rather than [Ar] 4s^2 3d^4.

questions.prompt: Which element has the ground-state configuration [Ne] 3s^2 3p^3? Give the name or the symbol.
hints: Add up all the electrons, including those hidden inside [Ne].
The total electron count is the atomic number.
questions.explanation: Neon accounts for 10 electrons and the rest add 2 + 3 = 5, giving 15 in total. Element 15 is phosphorus.

questions.prompt: How many UNPAIRED electrons does a ground-state nitrogen atom (Z = 7) have? Enter the number only.
hints: Draw the three 2p orbitals and place the electrons using Hund's rule.
Electrons occupy separate orbitals singly before they double up.
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is 1s^2 2s^2 2p^3. The three 2p electrons spread out one to each of the three 2p orbitals before any pairing begins, which is Hund's rule, so all three are unpaired.

commonErrors.message: Hund's rule spreads the three 2p electrons across all three 2p orbitals before any of them pair.
commonErrors.label: paired-too-early

questions.prompt: Copper (Z = 29) is an exception to the expected filling order. Write its actual ground-state configuration.
hints: The expected answer would be [Ar] 4s^2 3d^9. Move one electron to complete the d sublevel.
questions.explanation: The predicted configuration is [Ar] 4s^2 3d^9, but a filled d sublevel is more stable than a filled s, so one 4s electron shifts across to give [Ar] 4s^1 3d^10. Chromium behaves the same way, becoming [Ar] 4s^1 3d^5 for a half-filled d.

questions.prompt: How many valence electrons does a neutral aluminium atom (Z = 13) have? Enter the number only.
hints: Count only the electrons outside the [Ne] core.
questions.explanation: Aluminium is [Ne] 3s^2 3p^1, so the outermost level n = 3 holds 2 + 1 = 3 electrons. This is why aluminium forms Al^3+.

questions.prompt: Write the full electron configuration of the O^2- ion (oxygen is Z = 8).
hints: Start from neutral oxygen, then ADD two electrons because the charge is negative.
questions.explanation: Neutral oxygen is 1s^2 2s^2 2p^4. Gaining two electrons fills the 2p sublevel, giving 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6, which is the same configuration as neon. Reaching a noble-gas configuration is exactly what the octet rule describes.
